```{r load data, include=FALSE}

# combined mentee and mentor data 

df <-
  read_csv(here::here("processed data", "eval_final_combined_preprocessed.csv"),
           lazy = FALSE)



# load metadata
meta_tor <- read_csv(here::here("raw data", "metadata_eval_final_mentor.csv"), 
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"), lazy = FALSE) %>% 
  filter(old_variable != "NA") # remove the instruction variables



# load metadata 
meta_tee <- read_csv(here::here("raw data", "metadata_eval_final_mentee.csv"),

```


```{r code factors, include=FALSE}

df$role <- as.factor(df$role)

# turn all ratings variables into factors, regardless of whether they are from the mentee or mentor files
# use datapasta to do this!


cols <- c("networks_flinders",
  "advice_current",
  "advice_future",
  "enthusiastic",
  "recommendation_mentors",
  "recommendation_mentees",
  "second_rt_informative",
  "second_rt_valuable",
  "third_rt_informative",
  "third_rt_valuable")


# turn the cols columns into factors
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(across (all_of(cols), ~factor(., 
                                       levels = c("N/A", 
                                           "Strongly disagree",
                                           "Somewhat disagree",
                                           "Neither agree nor disagree",
                                           "Somewhat agree",
                                           "Strongly agree"))))

```

```{r total n, include=FALSE}

# The total n in the program has to be manually inputted to be used in the next section.

n_mentee <- 29
n_mentor <- 30
n_pairs <- 30

```
# Overview

The Researcher Mentoring Program for Early-Career Researchers for 2022 supported
`r n_pairs` mentee--mentor pairs. One of the mentees left Flinders University 
in the first half of the year; their mentor asked to be included in further
communication about the program, including the planned mid-point and end-of-year
evaluations. As such, a total of `r n_mentee` mentees and `r n_mentor` mentors were 
invited to complete this evaluation, which was open from Thursday 24 November 2022 to
Friday 16 December 2022. As I did not close the survey on Qualtrics, one mentor 
completed the evaluation after the close date (completed on December 19 2022).

Of those invited to complete the evaluation, `r nrow(df %>% filter(role == "mentee"))` 
mentees (`r round((nrow(df %>% filter(role == "mentee")) / n_mentee) *100, 0)`%) and
`r nrow(df %>% filter(role == "mentor"))` mentors 
(`r round((nrow(df %>% filter(role == "mentor")) / n_mentor) *100, 0)`%) 
completed the survey. 

```{r expectations data, include = TRUE}

expect_rate_mentee <- df %>% 
  filter (role == "mentee") %>% 
    dplyr::group_by (role, met_expectations) %>% 
  count()

expect_rate_mentor <- df %>% 
  filter (role == "mentor") %>% 
    dplyr::group_by (role, met_expectations) %>% 
  count()

# I need to split the comments up by role (because the pack_rows isn't working) & 
  # also give new numbers according to their role

tee_expect <- df %>%
  mutate(Participant = 1:n()) %>%
  filter(role %in% "mentee") %>%
  mutate(`Mentee Number` = 1:n()) %>%
  select (Participant, `Mentee Number`, role, expectations_comment) %>%
  filter (!is.na(expectations_comment))

tor_expect <- df %>%
  mutate(Participant = 1:n()) %>%
  filter(role %in% "mentor") %>%
  mutate(`Mentor Number` = 1:n()) %>% 
  select (Participant, `Mentor Number`, role, expectations_comment) %>%
  filter (!is.na(expectations_comment))


```
## Expectations

All respondents indicated that the program partly or fully met or exceeded their 
expectations. 

Specifically, of the `r expect_rate_mentor[[3]] %>% sum` mentors who responded,
`r expect_rate_mentor[[1,3]]` (`r round((expect_rate_mentor[[1,3]]/(expect_rate_mentor[[3]] %>% sum))*100,0)`%)
indicated that it exceeded their expectations and 
`r expect_rate_mentor[[2,3]]` (`r round((expect_rate_mentor[[2,3]]/(expect_rate_mentor[[3]] %>% sum))*100,0)`%)
reported that the program met their expectations. 
The mentors' explanations of how the program aligned with their expectations are shown in 
`r table_nums(name = "tor_expect", display = "cite")`. 

\

## Ratings from mentees and mentors

In the scaled-response questions, we asked eight questions that were common to the 
mentees and mentors. We use the term 'their partner' in the text below, but the 
actual question for the mentee referred to their mentor and for the mentor it referred
to their mentee. 


```{r creating tibbles for all rating responses for common questions, include = FALSE}

# Analyse the questions that are common to both mentees & mentors

# get total n to calculate percentages

total_n <- length(df$id)

# SELECT THE RATING COLUMNS & SAVE AS A TIBBLE I WANT TO SUMMARISE & PLOT USING THE RATING_SUMMARY FUNCTION

comm_rating <- df %>% 
  select( c("networks_flinders",
            "enthusiastic",
            "recommendation_mentees"))

# UPDATE THE COLUMNS PARAMETER WITH THE STRINGS FROM ABOVE

columns <- c("networks_flinders",
            "enthusiastic",
            "recommendation_mentees")

# RUN THE FUNCTION & APPLY TO ALL COLUMNS IN OUR DF

comm_ratings_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(columns, .f = function(column) {
	ratings_summary(comm_rating, column)
})

# remove the NA responses
comm_ratings_summary <- na.omit(comm_ratings_summary)

```


```{r creating agreement tibbles for common questions}

# calculate how many responded with the agree ratings. I use these in the 
  # text summaries later

# [breadcrumb: can I use apply for this too?? Who knows? I think I need to transpose it, 
  # so that's another problem for another day]

agree <- c("Strongly agree", "Somewhat agree")

network_agree <- comm_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "networks_flinders") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

enthusiastic_agree <- comm_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "enthusiastic") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

rec_mentees_agree <- comm_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "recommendation_mentees") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

```

Of these common questions, the numbers in parentheses indicate the percentage
of those who responded that either somewhat agreed or strongly agreed to each item:

  * This program is expanding their networks at Flinders University 
  (`r   sum(network_agree$percentage)`%).
  * They feel enthusiastic after meeting with their partner (`r   sum(enthusiastic_agree$percentage)`%).
  * They would recommend that their ECR colleagues participate as mentees (`r sum(rec_mentees_agree$percentage)`%).

`r fig_nums(name = "comm_ratings_summary", display = "cite")` shows a breakdown of ratings to these common questions.


## Ratings from mentees

In addition to the questions that were common to the mentees and mentors, we
asked questions that were unique to each group. Specifically, we asked the mentees
six unique questions. 

```{r create tibbles for rating responses for mentee-only questions, include = FALSE}

# Analyse the questions that are unique to mentees 

# Mentee-only questions

  # First, filter for mentee only

df_tee <- df %>% 
  filter(role == "mentee")

# get total n of mentees to calculate percentages
  # the function calls this 'total_n' so we have to use that object in the function

total_n <- length(df_tee$id)

# SELECT THE RATING COLUMNS & SAVE AS A TIBBLE I WANT TO SUMMARISE & PLOT USING THE RATINGS_SUMMARY FUNCTION

tee_ratings <- df_tee %>% 
  select( c("second_rt_informative", 
            "second_rt_valuable",
            "third_rt_informative", 
            "third_rt_valuable",
            "advice_current",
            "advice_future"
))

# UPDATE THE COLUMNS PARAMETER WITH THE STRINGS FROM ABOVE

columns <- c("second_rt_informative", 
            "second_rt_valuable",
            "third_rt_informative", 
            "third_rt_valuable",
            "advice_current",
            "advice_future"
)

# RUN THE FUNCTION & APPLY TO ALL COLUMNS IN OUR DF

tee_ratings_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(columns, .f = function(column) {
	ratings_summary(tee_ratings, column)
})

# remove the NA responses
tee_ratings_summary <- na.omit(tee_ratings_summary)

```


```{r create agreement tibbles for mentee-only questions}

# calculate how many responded with the agree ratings. I use these in the 
  # text summaries later

# [breadcrumb: can I use apply for this too?? Who knows? I think I need to transpose it, 
  # so that's another problem for another day]

agree <- c("Strongly agree", "Somewhat agree")

second_rt_informative_agree <- tee_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "second_rt_informative") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

second_rt_valuable_agree <- tee_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "second_rt_valuable") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

third_rt_informative_agree <- tee_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "third_rt_informative") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

third_rt_valuable_agree <- tee_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "third_rt_valuable") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

advice_current_agree <- tee_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "advice_current") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

advice_future_agree <- tee_ratings_summary %>%
  filter (rating_item == "advice_future") %>% 
  filter (rating %in% agree)

```


Of the mentee-only questions, the numbers in parentheses indicate the percentage
of those who responded that either somewhat agreed or strongly agreed to each item:

  * Their mentor is providing advice and/or guidance that will help them with their
  current aspirations (`r sum(advice_current_agree$percentage)`%).
  * Their mentor is providing advice and/or guidance that will help them with 
  their future research career (`r sum(advice_future_agree$percentage)`%). 
  * The second Mentee Roundtable was informative 
  (`r sum(second_rt_informative_agree$percentage)`%).
  * The second Mentee Roundtable was valuable 
  (`r sum(second_rt_valuable_agree$percentage)`%). 
  * The third Mentee Roundtable was informative 
  (`r sum(third_rt_informative_agree$percentage)`%).
  * The third Mentee Roundtable was valuable 
  (`r sum(third_rt_valuable_agree$percentage)`%). 

These lower ratings of agreement of the value and informativeness of the Mentee
Roundtables are explained by the lower attendance at the roundtables as the 
program progressed throughout the year (as evidenced by the high rate of "N/A" responses).

`r fig_nums(name = "tee_ratings_summary", display = "cite")` shows a breakdown of 
mentees' ratings to these questions.

\
`r fig_nums(name = "tee_ratings_summary")`

We also asked the mentors if they had any tips and tricks that they wanted to 
share with future mentors. 

```{r tips table, include = TRUE}

tips <- df %>% 
  filter(role == "mentor") %>% 
  select (id, tips) %>% 
  filter (!is.na(tips))

# I think i can delete this code because we want folks to be able to match the comments across the tables


kable(
  tips,
    booktabs = T, 
  escape = TRUE,
    format = "latex",
  longtable = T,
  align = c('cl'),
  linesep = "\\addlinespace",
  caption = "Mentors' tips and tricks for future mentors",
  col.names = c("Respondent", "Response")
  ) %>%
  column_spec (column = 2, width = "14cm") %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position", "repeat_header"), 
  full_width = FALSE)

```
